title: Tidewater Sync 2.4 – Command-line Guide
key_sentences: Tidewater Sync copies a directory tree to remote storage on a schedule.
This guide explains how to install the tool, write its configuration file and diagnose the most common failures.
The tool needs Python 3.10 or later.
Unknown keys are rejected so that typing mistakes are caught early.
Run tidewater sync once to copy the changes since the last run, or tidewater daemon to keep running on the configured schedule.
The process always finishes the file it is copying before it stops.
If the problem persists, attach the log file to your support request together with the output of tidewater --version.

tables.caption: Table 1: Configuration options
rows: Directory to read from. It must exist and be readable.
Destination, for example a bucket or an SFTP path.
When to run in daemon mode.
Days to keep old snapshots before they are deleted.

list_items.text: TIDEWATER_CONFIG – path of the configuration file
TIDEWATER_LOG_LEVEL – one of debug, info, warning or error
TIDEWATER_DRY_RUN – set to 1 to list actions without copying
1. Run again with the log level set to debug.
- Note the retry counter of the failed upload.
2. Check that the target is reachable from the machine that runs the tool.
3. Verify the credentials and the clock of the machine, because expired signatures are rejected.

code:
# tidewater.yaml
source: /srv/data/exports
target: s3://example-bucket/backups
schedule: "0 2 * * *"
retention_days: 30
exclude:
  - "*.tmp"
  - ".cache/"
